title: The Song of Innocence
subtitle: Slow down, child. I'm not going anywhere.

items.text: The Song of Innocence
Laplace Rehabilitation Center

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: She’s in a deep sleep. Unlike adults, who often relive traumatic memories during this time, children face the danger of never waking up from their dreams at all.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do we have a way to wake her up?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Was I not clear enough? This is a "condition," not an ordinary state of sleep. Forcibly waking her could cause serious brain trauma.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Aside from letting her little brain wake up on its own, there is no other solution.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: ...Such an out of control Arcanist ought to be subject to more stringent and regular checks.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: The LSCC's research on her grandfather's arm ring is still in the exploratory phase. It won't be of immediate help to her.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Moreover, the death records here show that her mother was hospitalized for the same reason.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: This is the "gift" that accompanies their family's Arcanism, a rare kind of hereditary illness.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Fortunately, though, we have a sample right here with us now. This should prove useful in treating Arcanist illnesses.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: You have indeed made a good deal with her grandfather, Vertin.
She presses a needle into Erick's wrist, and slowly releases the liquid within.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: This is 5 milliliters of Mandragora extract, a hemostatic and neural blocker. It will slow the worsening of her condition to maintain her vital signs for about 2–3 days, but it's far greater than the normal dose.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Even a carbuncle nearly 7 feet tall would be knocked unconscious by this. It’s commonly used in the black market for live critter dissection.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But aren't we supposed to be finding a way to wake her up?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Aside from the coma, she has other, more lethal issues.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: According to the blood dilution analysis report, her body is abnormally "expending" blood. Her veins are filled with blood-sucking parasites.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: The most conservative treatment is to first calm these "parasites."

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: As I’m sure you know, this is our last sample.
She returns the empty vial to the shelf.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I'll come back in 4 hours.
The medication quickly takes effect. Her breathing becomes lighter.
Outside, dark clouds gather. They are building up to a downpour.
The direct light is dazzling. Erick rubs her eyes. Her brain is on the verge of waking, but the sleepiness is unstoppable.
As she mutters incomprehensibly in her sleep, the softness of her blanket pulls her deeper into her dreams.
Her body instinctively rolls away from the light—
"Thud!"

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Ouch! That hurts...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Oww, my head! It's going to swell up as big as a bar of soap.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Huh? Wait, this is...!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: My room?!
The storybook lies open there on the floor.
The carpet is sticky with chewing gum, smelly socks crumpled on the ground. All the familiar messiness—

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: My little sleepyhead, has winter finally passed?

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Harald?! Is this real?! Wait, I’ll pull a hair to see if I’m dreaming...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Ouch... Ow! That really hurts!

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: Go wash your face quickly, and grab your helmet and weapons. Your dad's already gone to pick up your little sailors.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: But, but why...

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: Oh, have you forgotten? Today is the "Victory Party" I told you about. I’m so impressed that you’ve completed such a perilous journey. What a feat! I'm proud of you, child.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Right... that sounds familiar...

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: Looks like that fall really did a number on your head... We'll wait for you downstairs, child.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: Remember to tidy up your room a bit.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Okay, okay! You’re starting to sound like nagging Old John!
She scratches her messy hair, opens the wardrobe, and starts rummaging around...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: But when did I get home...? I don't remember a thing.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Where was I before—

items.speaker: Little Sailors
items.text: Welcome home, Erick!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Oh! Sailors, you scared me!
The children swarm around her, holding her hands, crowding her onto a throne draped with bearskin.

items.speaker: Snotty Buck
items.text: Erick, I heard you went to a place full of witches!

items.speaker: Jason “the Slob”
items.text: They could go anywhere unimpeded and could even predict exam questions! And they had monsters that could eat a tire whole in one bite.

items.speaker: Little Sailors
items.text: Is it true?! Is it true?!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Calm down, sailors; it wasn’t as scary as that. Though it was certainly perilous, the witches there were actually quite reasonable...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: And those monsters, wow, you have to see them to believe it. I can't even begin to describe how scary they looked.

items.speaker: Little Sailors
items.text: Tell us, tell us!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: So, listen up, that place...
A grand story begins anew, the children gasp in horror yet are unable to pull themselves away. They crane their necks like a little herd of giraffes.
Old John clatters in the kitchen, occasionally glancing at his daughter before going back to stirring his pot of thick soup.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: There, I had two of the greatest sailors. They were...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: They were...
The children continue to stare at her.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Sorry, it’s strange... I can't remember a thing.
As if a stone is suddenly lodged in her throat, she can no longer continue the story.
Hey, Erick. Hey!
A voice seems to push through a thin membrane.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Did you guys... hear something?

items.speaker: Jason “the Slob”
items.text: Nope, I didn't hear anything.

items.speaker: Snotty Buck
items.text: Heh-heh, I heard it! Jason, you bad boy, you ripped a stealthy one!

items.speaker: Jason “the Slob”
items.text: Y-You’re talking nonsense!
They scrap it out, first Jason on top of Buck, then Buck targeting Jason’s ticklish spot.
They grab their desired pillows to start a pillow fight on the sofa.
The living room becomes a chaotic playground, with children cheering and laughing uproariously.
Pfft, pfft!
Shh, don't bring "it" over here... be quiet, you idiot.
Two tiny figures press against the window, whispering.
But apart from Erick, no one else seems to notice them. She approaches the window and peers out.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: You two idiots, what are you doing standing there at my doorstep? Come in, all my friends are welcome!
...But w-we can't go in, Erick.
"It" is coming...
When "it" arrives, it takes away all joy. "It" will take away the candy and amusement parks, the fun of running away, and your prized little wooden sword.
"It" will eat your heart, so you'll never feel excitement again. Your feet will feel like they’re chained, and your head will feel like it’s carrying a hundred gold pieces, too heavy to lift again.
Eventually, you'll start forgetting, forgetting the great stories and the treasures at your fingertips.
We don't want that; we can't let "it" in.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Don't worry, guys, I'll knock "it" down before it can even take a breath!
But it's our turn to protect you now, Jarl!
Shh, shh! "It" is coming, run!
The figures outside the window flee fast.
She quickly opens the window.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: ...Strange, what's going on?
The setting sun casts its rays, hitting her face and the green lawn outside. The sprinkler is hissing.
But there's no one there.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: ...This is a frightening monster, child.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: I mean... yes, I do know of it.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: What kind of monster is it? I didn't even see what it looks like...

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: Do you remember the museum ticket seller, the lady who always picked you up?

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Ms. Sigrid? Oh, her face was long and sour, her voice croaky like an old crow. If she caught you doing something she didn’t like, you were in for a serious paddling.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: The worst part was having to listen to her endless lectures afterward. "Children should behave themselves." "When I was your age..." Blah, blah, blah. I'd rather walk the plank!

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: Do you remember the day you climbed the "World Tree" and the carvings you found at the top?

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "The Eagle Feeder tops them all."

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "The next kid to read these words will become the new master of the World Tree."

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: It was Ms. Sigrid who carved those words.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: When she was your age, she ran faster and jumped further than any boy in the village. But, none of the boys wanted to admit that a girl could best them.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: So, one day, they dared her to climb the World Tree, the tallest tree in the village. If she failed, then she would have to say they had been letting her win all along.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: We all know what happened next.
He sighs deeply, spreading his hands.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: But, adults always think a girl running fast or getting sun-tanned... is not a good thing.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: So, one day, the Eagle Feeder met this monster. At first, they were evenly matched, palm against claw, stubbornness against obstinacy.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: But eventually, she wore out.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: Her heart was torn to shreds by that monster, but no one ever saw her shed a tear.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: —And then she became Ms. Sigrid, the gloomy ticket seller who’s always telling off kids.
Erick, sitting on the bed's edge, lowers her head uneasily.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: ...I’m so sorry for what I said about her. She was a courageous hero. That monster... must have been truly scary...

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: Yes. It has no name, and no one has ever seen it with their own eyes. You must be careful.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: But now, it's relentlessly pursuing my two sailors... They led the monster away to protect me.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: They are brave too.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: But what should I do? what should I do? Harald, can you help me?
She looks up eagerly, her eyes wide with hope.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: I'm afraid not, child... My hands are too big, and the monster too small; my footsteps are too heavy, and its too light.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: Only a child could defeat it, and only a child could be defeated by it.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: But what if I lose to it? If I become like Ms. Sigrid... will you still love me the same?

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: No matter what you become.
He holds the child's arms until she stops trembling and raises her head.
It felt like she was gazing into his eyes a thousand, ten thousand times over.

items.speaker: Harald
items.text: I'll be waiting for you.
Her palms no longer tremble, her steps grow lighter.
She runs down the hallway.
Runs down the stairs.
Runs through the bustling living room.

items.speaker: Jason “the Slob”
items.text: Erick, where are you going? Are you leaving the party?

items.speaker: Snotty Buck
items.text: You can't go, we've been waiting ages for you. Look, we even brought a popcorn machine from the shop!

items.speaker: Little Sailors
items.text: We want to hear your stories about your grand adventure, about the treasures you brought back!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Sorry...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: I miss you all and those good old days of adventuring...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: But I've made a promise to two other sailors you don’t know. I can't abandon them...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Sailors, I'll come back for you, but not now.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Jason, sorry... I'll return your homework later. You can blame it on me.

items.speaker: Jason “the Slob”
items.text: ...Don't worry, boss. My behind is battle-hardened. Even if the teacher comes with a branding iron, I won't utter a sound!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: And Buck, if Nasty Abel still bothers you while I'm gone... tell him to stop acting smug; Jarl Erick will settle the score.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: If he wants more trouble, take Jason's hellhound "Garm" over there.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Remember, it only eats sturgeon fish that have been left out for three days and three nights.

items.speaker: Snotty Buck
items.text: Thank you...
The children watch her, like a farewell choir.
She grabs the doorknob, feeling the cold metal in her palm.
Suddenly, a hand reaches out to stop her.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Old John... don't block the way, this isn't—
—He wraps both hands around her shoulders.
He ruffles her golden hair. His embrace makes it hard for her to breathe.
But she doesn't resist, she just allows him to hold her tightly, so tightly.
Eventually, he lets go.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: I have to go.
She turns the doorknob.
The dawn light spills through the gaps in the trees, illuminating her in patterns.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Goodbye, Dad.
TO BE CONTINUED…
